symbols.name: \mathcal U
symbols.space: The latent state space with \(2\le r=\lvert\mathcal U\rvert\).

symbols.name: \mathcal W
symbols.space: The proxy state space with \(m=\lvert\mathcal W\rvert\ge r\).

symbols.name: \mathcal Y
symbols.space: The outcome state space with \(\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert\ge2\).

symbols.name: \mathcal G
symbols.def: The graph has arrows \(E\to U\), \(U\to W\), \(U\to X\), \(U\to Y\), \(W\to Y\), and \(X\to Y\).

symbols.name: \mathcal M
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M=(\pi,S,M,a,f,q)\) is Markov relative to \(\mathcal G\).

symbols.name: P_{\mathcal M}
symbols.type: source full-data law induced by the SCM

symbols.name: Q_{\mathcal M}
symbols.type: target law induced by the SCM

symbols.name: \mathbb M
symbols.type: triangular array of finite latent-shift SCMs
symbols.def: \(\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge2}\) with \(\mathcal M_n\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) for every \(n\ge2\).

symbols.name: n_s(n)
symbols.role: source sample size in triangular-array row \(n\)

symbols.name: n_t(n)
symbols.role: target sample size in triangular-array row \(n\)

symbols.name: P_{O,n}
symbols.def: The observed law of \((E,W,X,Y)\) induced by \(\mathcal M_n\).

symbols.name: \sigma_{r_0}
symbols.def: \(\sigma_{r_0}(H)\) is the \(r_0\)-th largest singular value of \(H\).

symbols.name: H_{r_0}
symbols.def: Because \(q\) already denotes the target latent mixture, write \(\bar q=\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert)\) and adopt \(\sigma_{\bar q+1}(H)=0\). Fix once and for all, for every \(H\), a possibly noncomputable selector of an orthonormal eigenbasis \(u_1^{\star}(H),\ldots,u_m^{\star}(H)\) of \(HH^{\top}\), ordered by nonincreasing eigenvalue, with one fixed choice inside every tied eigenspace. Put \(P_{r_0}^{\star}(H)=\sum_{j=1}^{r_0}u_j^{\star}(H)u_j^{\star}(H)^{\top}\), \(H_{r_0}^{\star}=P_{r_0}^{\star}(H)H\), and \(H_{r_0}=H_{r_0}^{\star}\). If \(\sigma_{r_0}(H)>\sigma_{r_0+1}(H)\), the retained subspace, \(P_{r_0}^{\star}(H)\), and \(H_{r_0}\) are independent of the fixed within-tie selector.

symbols.name: V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)
symbols.type: nonnegative population delta-method variance on the strict-cutoff-gap region
symbols.def: When \(\sigma_{r_0}(H_x)>\sigma_{r_0+1}(H_x)\), let \(\Gamma_{x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\) be the covariance matrix of the joint source-and-target multinomial limit for \((H_x,z_{x,y},b)\), with allocation factors \(p^{-1}\) and \((1-p)^{-1}\), and define \(V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)=D\phi_{r_0}(H_x,z_{x,y},b)\,\Gamma_{x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\,D\phi_{r_0}(H_x,z_{x,y},b)^{\top}\), where \(D\phi_{r_0}\) is the ordinary derivative on this selector-independent region. The population variance is not defined outside this region.

symbols.name: \mathcal A_p
symbols.type: admissible class of two-sample triangular arrays

standard.name: Invariant mechanisms under latent distribution shift

assumptions.condition: Every entry of \(\pi\), \(S\), \(M\), \(a\), \(f\), and \(q\) is strictly positive.

standard.name: Finite proxy completeness through full column rank

assumptions.condition: The observations \(O_1^s,\ldots,O_{n_s}^s\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P_O\).
The observations \(W_1^t,\ldots,W_{n_t}^t\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(b\).
The sequences \(n_s(n)\) and \(n_t(n)\) are deterministic, \(n_s(n)+n_t(n)=n\) for every \(n\), \(n\to\infty\), and \(n_s(n)/n\to p\in(0,1)\).
For every \(n\), the observations \(O^s_{1,n},\ldots,O^s_{n_s(n),n}\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P_{O,n}\).
For every \(n\), the observations \(W^t_{1,n},\ldots,W^t_{n_t(n),n}\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(b_n\).
For every \(n\), the row-\(n\) target proxy law satisfies \(b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n})\).

novel.justification: The condition is observable and holds when the target proxy distribution is a linear mixture of the treatment-specific source proxy distributions, including applications with deficient global source rank.

assumptions.condition: The fixed source moment matrix satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(H_x)=r_0\).
The smallest retained singular value satisfies \(\sigma_{r_0}(H_x)\ge c\).

standard.name: Singular-value separation on a fixed-rank submodel

assumptions.condition: The fixed target proxy vector satisfies \(b\in\operatorname{col}(H_x)\).

standard.name: Identified loading in the moment column space

assumptions.condition: The minimum over all source observed cells and target proxy cells satisfies \(\min\bigl(\{P_O(e,w,x,y):e\in\mathcal E,w\in\mathcal W,x\in\mathcal X,y\in\mathcal Y\}\cup\{b_w:w\in\mathcal W\}\bigr)\ge\eta\).
The population delta-method variance satisfies \(V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak M_{+}
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{+}=\{\mathcal M=(\pi,S,M,a,f,q):\mathcal M\text{ satisfies the latent-shift factorization, strict primitive positivity, and }\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\}\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak F(\mathcal D)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}:\mathcal M\text{ induces exactly the supplied }P_O\text{ and }b\}\).

definitions.name: f^{(t)}
definitions.construction: Fix \(h\in\mathcal H_x(\mathcal D)\), put \(v=M^{\top}h\), choose \(w_{\star}\in\mathcal W\) and \(y^{\circ}\ne y\), and set \(f^{(t)}_{x,y}(u,w_{\star})=f_{x,y}(u,w_{\star})+t v_u/M_{w_{\star}u}\), \(f^{(t)}_{x,y^{\circ}}(u,w_{\star})=f_{x,y^{\circ}}(u,w_{\star})-t v_u/M_{w_{\star}u}\); every other cell equals \(f\).

definitions.name: \widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}
definitions.construction: Let \(L=m\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+m\), \(r_s=\sqrt{\log(2L/\alpha)/(2n_s)}\), and \(r_t=\sqrt{\log(2L/\alpha)/(2n_t)}\). Define \(\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}=\{\vartheta\in[0,1]:\exists\kappa\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert},\ \lVert\widehat H_x\kappa-\widehat b\rVert_{\infty}\le r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1+r_t,\ |\widehat z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa-\vartheta|\le r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1\}\).

definitions.name: \mathcal A_p
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal A_p=\{\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge2}:\mathbb M\text{ obeys the fixed-proportion allocation and row-wise source and target i.i.d. sampling conditions, and }b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n})\text{ for every }n\ge2\}\). No restriction is imposed on changes in \(\operatorname{rank}(B_{x,n})\), singularity of the joint multinomial covariance, or divergence of \(d_{x,n}\).

definitions.name: \mathcal R_{r_0,c,\eta}
definitions.construction: For \(1\le r_0\le\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert)\) and fixed \(c,\eta>0\), \(\mathcal R_{r_0,c,\eta}=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}:\operatorname{rank}(H_x)=r_0,\ \sigma_{r_0}(H_x)\ge c,\ b\in\operatorname{col}(H_x),\text{ every source and target cell is at least }\eta,\text{ and }V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta\}\).

definitions.name: \phi_{r_0}
definitions.construction: For \(H\in\mathbb R^{m\times\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\), \(z\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), define the scalar function \(\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)=z^{\top}H_{r_0}^{\dagger}b\), where \(H_{r_0}=H^{\star}_{r_0}\) is the selector-based Gram-spectral truncation fixed in the definition of \(H_{r_0}\). Thus \(\phi_{r_0}\) is single valued at tied cutoffs. If \(\sigma_{r_0}(H)>\sigma_{r_0+1}(H)\), the retained subspace is unique, so both \(H_{r_0}\) and \(\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)\) are independent of the fixed within-tie selector.

definitions.name: \widehat V_n
definitions.construction:
Put \(\widehat T_n=(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n)\), and let \(\widehat\Gamma_n\) be the plug-in covariance matrix of \(\sqrt n\,\widehat T_n\), formed from the joint source multinomial covariance and the target multinomial covariance with allocation factors \(p^{-1}\) and \((1-p)^{-1}\). The totalized plug-in variance is
\[
\widehat V_n=
\begin{cases}
D\phi_{r_0}(\widehat T_n)\,\widehat\Gamma_n\,D\phi_{r_0}(\widehat T_n)^{\top},
&\sigma_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n})>\sigma_{r_0+1}(\widehat H_{x,n}),\\
0,&\sigma_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n})\le\sigma_{r_0+1}(\widehat H_{x,n}),
\end{cases}
\]
where \(D\phi_{r_0}\) is the ordinary derivative of the selector-independent functional on the strict-cutoff-gap region and \(\sigma_{\bar q+1}=0\) for \(\bar q=\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert)\). The second line is the fixed nonnegative fallback.

definitions.name: d_H
definitions.construction: For nonempty \(C,D\subseteq[0,1]\), \(d_H(C,D)=\max\{\sup_{\xi\in C}\inf_{\zeta\in D}|\xi-\zeta|,\sup_{\zeta\in D}\inf_{\xi\in C}|\xi-\zeta|\}\), the Euclidean Hausdorff distance.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\), \(B_x=MR_x\), \(b=Mq\), \(c_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}R_x\), and \(\theta_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}q\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\). Moreover, every \(\lambda\in\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) and its unconditional weight map \(\kappa\) satisfy \(H_x\kappa=b\) and \(z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa=\theta_{x,y}\).
statements.justification: This reduction isolates the observed span and the latent adjustment functional without identifying the latent factorization.
statements.gap: Iglesias-Alonso et al. use the same factorization under full source rank; the lemma is supporting algebra and carries no standalone novelty claim.
statements.consumer: The exact identification theorem and both inference constructions use these four identities.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\ne\varnothing\) and \(b\notin\operatorname{col}(B_x)\). For every baseline \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\), every \(y\in\mathcal Y\), and every \(h\in\mathcal H_x(\mathcal D)\), there is \(\varepsilon>0\) such that replacing \(f\) by \(f^{(t)}\) yields \(\mathcal M_t\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\) for all \(|t|<\varepsilon\), while \(\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M_t)-\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M)=t h^{\top}b\). Hence the compatible values of \(\theta_{x,y}\) contain a nondegenerate open interval around the baseline value.
statements.justification: The observable separator is lifted to a positive SCM perturbation that preserves every supplied source joint cell, not merely the balancing equations.
statements.gap: Zhang et al. characterize constancy on an abstract bridge fiber, and Iglesias-Alonso et al. give a single counterexample with a rank-deficient proxy channel; neither proves this input-specific full-law converse while retaining an injective proxy channel.
statements.consumer: A failed target-span audit for an Expedia hotel becomes a causal nonidentification certificate rather than a numerical-rank warning.

statements.statement: For every supplied \(\mathcal D=(P_O,b)\) with \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\ne\varnothing\), every \(x\in\mathcal X\), and every \(y\in\mathcal Y\), the target interventional probability \(\theta_{x,y}\) is constant on \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\) if and only if \(b\in\operatorname{col}(B_x)\). On the identified branch, \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\ne\varnothing\) and every \(\lambda\in\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) satisfies \(\theta_{x,y}=c_{x,y}\lambda\); in particular, \(c_{x,y}\lambda=c_{x,y}\lambda'\) for all \(\lambda,\lambda'\in\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\).
statements.justification: This is the exact target-specific frontier: deficient source rank is harmless precisely for target proxy mixtures already spanned by the observed source mixtures.
statements.gap: Iglesias-Alonso et al. prove sufficiency under full latent source rank, Zhang et al. prove abstract null-space annihilation, and Rahiminasab et al. require full rank over latent-equivalence-class mixtures for prediction; none states this causal full-observed-law if-and-only-if frontier.
statements.consumer: The Expedia hotel-ranking analysis can retain target hotels whose price distributions are balanceable even when the global source-diversity rank condition fails.

statements.statement: The target-span condition strictly weakens the source-rank condition of Iglesias-Alonso et al. Under \(\operatorname{rank}(B_x)=r\), one has \(\operatorname{col}(B_x)=\operatorname{col}(M)\) and therefore \(b\in\operatorname{col}(B_x)\). The explicit construction \(\mathcal M^{\star}\) belongs to \(\mathfrak M_{+}\), has \(\operatorname{rank}(B_x)=2<3=r\) for both treatments, and satisfies \(b\in\operatorname{col}(B_x)\), so the intervention law remains identified outside the published full-rank regime.
statements.justification: The exact rational witness establishes a nonempty identifiable region excluded by the anchor's global rank requirement.
statements.gap: Iglesias-Alonso et al., Assumption 1 and Theorem 1, require rank at least the latent cardinality; their Appendix B.2 weakens the proxy channel rather than exhibiting this complete-proxy, deficient-source-rank success regime.
statements.consumer: The result licenses target-specific balancing in applications with fewer informative source contrasts than latent strata.

statements.statement: If \(b\in\operatorname{col}(B_x)\), then for every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\), every sample size pair \((n_s,n_t)\), and every \(0<\alpha<1\), \(\mathbb P_{\mathcal M}^{\,n_s,n_t}\{\theta_{x,y}\in\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\). The bound is uniform over all positive cell probabilities, all ranks and nonzero singular values of \(B_x\), and all magnitudes of balancing vectors; the set may be empty for incompatible samples and may equal \([0,1]\).
statements.justification: Simultaneous concentration and projection give honest causal coverage without estimating rank or dividing by a weak singular value.
statements.gap: Iglesias-Alonso et al. use pointwise Wald calibration under full rank, while Dufour and Taamouti project AR regions in linear IV; this theorem gives a finite-sample two-multinomial transport analogue with unrestricted balancing weights.
statements.consumer: The Expedia analysis can report a valid, possibly nonshrinking set when hotel-source balance is weak instead of a misleading short Wald interval.

sampling_model.design: The source full-data law remains \(P_{\mathcal M}\), while observed inference uses the independent product law \(\mathbb P_{\mathcal M}^{\,n_s,n_t}=P_O^{\otimes n_s}\otimes b^{\otimes n_t}\). For the finite-sample theorem, there are \(n_s\) source draws from \(P_O(E,W,X,Y)\) and \(n_t\) target proxy draws from \(b=Q(W)\). For the studentized question, deterministic sequences satisfy \(n_s(n)+n_t(n)=n\), \(n\to\infty\), and \(n_s(n)/n\to p\in(0,1)\), with row law \(\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}=P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}\).
sampling_model.units: At triangular-array row \(n\), source observations \(O^s_{i,n}\), \(1\le i\le n_s(n)\), record \((E,W,X,Y)\), and target observations \(W^t_{j,n}\), \(1\le j\le n_t(n)\), record only \(W\); the two row-wise i.i.d. samples are independent.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is observational in the source law, and the causal query intervenes at a fixed \(x\in\mathcal X\).
sampling_model.overlap: Primitive source and target probabilities are strictly positive. The finite-sample theorem imposes no lower bound on a singular value of \(B_x\) and no bound on \(\lVert\lambda\rVert\) or \(\lVert\kappa\rVert\); the studentized class \(\mathcal A_p\) likewise permits changing rank, singular joint multinomial covariance, and diverging minimum-norm balancing weights.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The finite-sample set uses \(\widehat H_x\), \(\widehat z_{x,y}\), and \(\widehat b\). At row \(n\), the studentized handle uses the indexed empirical frequencies \(\widehat H_{x,n}\), \(\widehat z_{x,y,n}\), and \(\widehat b_n\), and projects over unrestricted \(\kappa\). On \(\mathcal R_{r_0,c,\eta}\), the benchmark \(\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}=\phi_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n)\) uses rank-\(r_0\) truncated SVD, and \(\widehat V_n\) plugs the joint source and target multinomial covariances into the delta method with allocation factors \(p^{-1}\) and \((1-p)^{-1}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Assumption 1 and Theorem 1 identify the target intervention distribution when \(\operatorname{rank}(P(W\mid E,x))\ge\lvert\mathcal U\rvert\).
Proposition 2.3 identifies a linear functional of a nonunique bridge if and only if its loading annihilates the conditional-expectation operator null space.
Theorem 3 identifies a target predictor when source environments have full rank over proxy-induced latent-equivalence-class mixtures.
Theorems 4.1 and 5.1--5.3 characterize boundedness and scalar projections of Anderson--Rubin quadric confidence sets in linear structural models.
Theorem 6.1 gives nominal asymptotic size for singularity-robust full-vector AR tests, while Theorem 9.1 treats subvectors under additional nuisance regularity.

Uniform subvector-GMM inference profiles nuisance parameters across identification regimes, but its theory does not provide a projected test over an unrestricted, changing-rank balancing fiber with singular two-sample multinomial covariance.
Theorems 1--2 give proxy-based bounds without completeness in a single-domain proximal-confounding model.
Discrete SCM compatibility and sharp causal bounds can be reduced to polynomial programs with valid anytime outer bounds.

tldr: A target intervention law can remain identified even when source environments do not span the latent state space. In the strictly positive finite latent-shift SCM, injectivity of the unknown proxy channel turns the observable condition \(b=Q(W)\in\operatorname{col}(B_x)\), with \(B_x=P_O(W\mid E,x)\), into the exact identification frontier. Every solution of \(B_x\lambda=b\) gives the same functional \(c_{x,y}\lambda\). Off the span, an observed separator lifts to a proxy-stratum outcome perturbation that keeps the full source law and target proxy law fixed while moving the causal effect through an interval. A concentration-calibrated Anderson--Rubin-style projection set has finite-sample coverage without rank or weight bounds; uniformly informative studentized calibration under changing rank and singular covariance is stated as the first-class open problem.

project_justification.gap: Iglesias-Alonso et al. require full source rank and lose identification in their counterexample by making the proxy channel noninjective. Zhang et al. settle constancy of abstract bridge functionals, and Rahiminasab et al. use full source rank over proxy-equivalence classes for prediction. None gives the target-specific causal if-and-only-if result over the full observed-law SCM fiber with an injective proxy channel.
project_justification.niche: The target proxy mixture may lie in the span of deficient source proxy mixtures. That observable, target-specific geometry is enough for the causal functional even though neither the latent source mixture nor the balancing vector is unique.
project_justification.fill: The project proves sufficiency, solution independence, and an input-specific positive full-law converse; supplies an exact rational rank-deficient success witness; and attaches finite-sample projection coverage plus a sharply stated studentized weak-rank inference question.

related_work: Iglesias-Alonso et al. (2025, Assumption 1, Theorem 1, Appendix A.1, and Appendix B.2) define the same graph, observed-data pattern, target intervention law, reduced estimator, and Expedia application. Their theorem uses full latent source rank, while their failure construction makes \(P(W\mid U)\) rank deficient. Zhang et al. (2023, Proposition 2.3 and Lemma 2.4) show that a linear functional is unique on a nonunique bridge fiber exactly under null-space annihilation and distinguish identification from root-\(n\) estimability. The present proposal treats that algebra as an input and adds the causal realizability converse preserving every supplied joint cell. Rahiminasab et al. (2026, Definition 3 and Theorems 2--3) span latent-equivalence-class operators to identify a target predictor; their condition is global source rank at the quotient level and their target is predictive rather than interventional. Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2018, Theorem 1 and Examples 1--2) establish the foundational finite proxy-rank identification argument, while Shpitser, Wood-Doughty, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2023, Assumption 2.5 and Theorems 1 and 5) extend bridge identification graphically under sequential completeness. Tsai et al. (2024, Proposition 4.3 and Appendix B.3) use multi-domain proxy bridges for target prediction under full latent posterior rank. Dufour and Taamouti (2005, Theorems 4.1 and 5.1--5.3) motivate full-region inversion followed by scalar projection. Andrews and Guggenberger (2019, Equations 4.5--4.9 and Theorems 6.1 and 9.1) motivate retaining stochastic moment directions and separately enforcing nonstochastic identities, but their subvector result does not allow the present unbounded, changing-rank balancing fiber. Bennett et al. (2023, Theorem 1 and the functional strong-identification theorem) motivate a later regularity frontier for target functionals of weak inverse nuisances. Ghassami, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2023, Theorems 1--2 and the LogSumExp inference section) and Duarte et al. (2024, the polynomialization theorem and anytime algorithm) bound different incomplete-proxy or general finite-SCM classes; they do not characterize this shared-channel transport fiber.
technical_internal_limitation: Strict positivity of the primitive outcome kernel is load-bearing for the necessity theorem. If outcome probabilities may lie on the boundary, an observed all-zero response slice can identify \(\theta_{x,y}=0\) even off the target span. Proxy-channel injectivity is likewise load-bearing for sufficiency: with two identical proxy columns, the target proxy law can be unchanged while the target latent mixture and causal effect move. The population span condition is not consistently decidable by a hard sample-rank threshold on deficient-rank manifolds. The studentized singularity-robust projection theorem remains open and is not implied by the finite-sample concentration set.
honest_scope: The headline theorem concerns finite state spaces, an unknown full-column-rank proxy channel, unrestricted strictly positive response kernels with the displayed \(W\to Y\) edge, source observations of \((E,W,X,Y)\), and target observations of \(W\) only. It does not identify the latent factorization or require nonnegative balancing weights. Under full source rank it reduces to the Iglesias-Alonso et al. functional. When \(b\notin\operatorname{col}(B_x)\), the proposal proves non-singleton identification but does not claim sharp endpoints. The concentration projection set is honest but can be nonshrinking; informative uniform studentization, off-span sharp bounds, continuous proxies, and incomplete proxy channels remain separate questions.
